stories.headline: Allen and Mahomes renew their thrilling rivalry as the Bills host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night
stories.summary: — Sorry, Steve Spagnuolo. Josh Allen has no plans of going anywhere, any time soon.
stories.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- — Sorry, Steve Spagnuolo. Josh Allen has no plans of going anywhere, any time soon.


The Bills quarterback delivered some bad news to Kansas City's defensive coordinator after Spagnuolo this week joked about hoping Allen would have hung up his cleats by now.


“Not retired yet,” the smiling 30-year-old Allen said. “Hopefully, we have a long time before then.”


Spagnuolo spoke out of respect, while assessing the headaches the NFL’s 2024 MVP poses with his strong arm and threat to run.


“It just seems like when he plays the Kansas City Chiefs, he’s on fire. He becomes Superman,” Spagnuolo said. “The challenge with Josh is not only his physical challenge but it’s his mental challenge, and that’s why I was hoping he would hang up the shoes and we wouldn’t have to play him again.”


The same could be said about the Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes, the two-time NFL MVP and three-time Super Bowl winner, who has been no slouch against the Bills either.


Two of the NFL’s top quarterbacks take the field in Orchard Park, New York, on Thursday night to renew a thrilling must-see-TV rivalry and a highly anticipated Thanksgiving holiday showdown between AFC contenders. The Bills lead the conference at 9-1; and the Chiefs are 8-2.


Allen and Mahomes take top billing in their 11th meeting in seven seasons.


Allen owns the regular-season edge in going 5-1, with five straight wins. Mahomes is 4-0 against Buffalo in the playoffs, including two AFC championship game wins.


The two have combined for 51 touchdowns (41 passing, 10 rushing) and 5,288 yards passing. The only thing that may slow their production is weather, with rain and chilly temperatures in the forecast — not that conditions have stopped them before.


“When you look at quarterbacks like those two, it’s the amount of times you can be right and still lose the rep,” Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said. “I mean, you can trick them ... and you feel like you’ve got them trapped, and they get out of trouble.”


The added challenge for Buffalo is the Chiefs having rediscovered their running attack. The tandem of Kenneth Walker, who will miss his third straight game with a groin injury, and rookie Emmett Johnson are a major part of the reason the Chiefs have one of the top offenses in the league.


Though a Super Bowl isn’t on the line on Thursday, playoff seeding is. And the outing also represents an litmus test for both teams.


The Chiefs are 1-2 against opponents entering Week 12 with winning records, with their lone victory coming against Denver to open the season.


While the Bills count wins against Detroit, Minnesota and the Rams, they’ve spent the past four outings feasting on backup and third-string quarterbacks.


“I feel like that (narrative) is kind of off-putting a little bit,” linebacker Bradley Chubb said. “All we got to do is prove it to ourselves, man. And we know who we are.”


Bills cornerback Tre’Davious White takes a big-picture approach in what could be his final chance to be part of an Allen-Mahomes showdown.


“What separates these two is having that immense amount of pressure on each them, and every weekend able to go out there and perform when everybody’s looking,” the 31-year-old said. “We’re watching two of the greats in modern time. ... So I hope fans really appreciate the game and appreciate what’s going on.”


Need to know
Kansas City (8-2) at Buffalo (9-1).


When/where to watch: Thursday, 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC.


Latest odds: Bills by 2 1/2


Against the spread: Chiefs 6-4; Bills 8-2.


Last week: Chiefs beat Cardinals 34-7; Bills beat Dolphins 26-9.


Last meeting: Bills beat Chiefs 28-21 on Nov. 2, 2025, at Orchard Park.


Series record: Bills lead 31-26-1.


Matchup to watch
Allen vs. Mahomes. The Bills passing attack has improved with the offseason addition of DJ Moore who, when healthy, has become Allen’s favorite option. He has 31 catches for 466 yards and a team-leading four TDs receiving in essentially six full games. Mahomes has returned to form since offseason knee surgery. And he’s incorporating a new playmaker in Josh Downs, who has eight catches for 112 yards and a TD in two games since being acquired in a trade with Indianapolis.


Stats and stuff
— In their past 10 meetings, the Bills have outscored the Chiefs by a combined 270-264, with six outings decided by one-score margins.


— The Bills have a chance to open 10-1 or better for just the fourth time in team history, and first since a 10-1 start in 1991.


— Buffalo hasn’t trailed since the second quarter of a 33-30 win at Las Vegas on Oct. 18.


— The Bills haven’t allowed a touchdown since the first quarter of Buffalo’s 36-10 win over Baltimore on Nov. 1.


— Allen has thrown five TD passes and been intercepted five times in his past four starts.


— Mahomes has two or more TDs passing with no interceptions in his past four starts.


— The Chiefs are in position to open a season 9-2 or better for the sixth time under coach Andy Reid and 11th time in team history.


— Kansas City has matched a team record by winning each of its past three games by 21 or more points.


— Travis Kelce has 99 career catches of 25 yards or longer, tying Rob Gronkowski for most by an NFL tight end.


------

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United, Barcelona eye USMNT's Mathis Albert
stories.summary: Both Manchester United and Barcelona are reportedly looking at signing Borussia Dortmund's Mathis Albert. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United and Barcelona want to sign United States winger Mathis Albert from Borussia Dortmund, while United captain Bruno Fernandes, who is out of contract at the end of the season, is a target for Juventus. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Barcelona have stepped up their interest in Borussia Dortmund and USMNT winger Mathis Albert, TEAMtalk reports. The race to sign the 17-year-old is already gaining momentum, and he is keen to play more regularly than he currently is under Niko Kovac, having got just 38 minutes in the Bundesliga so far this season. Albert has previously turned down approaches from Manchester City, Barcelona and Bayern Munich, while Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal and Liverpool have also monitored him.

- Juventus have expressed an interest in signing Manchester United attacking midfielder Bruno Fernandes as a free agent in the summer, according to Tuttosport. They will face competition from AC Milan, who will try to reunite the 32-year-old with coach Ruben Amorim.It is felt as though the summer isn't the time for Fernandes to move to MLS or Saudi Arabia. Fernandes addressed his future on Tuesday by saying: "For us to start winning games and then we can start speaking about a contract." Inter Milan's Hakan Çalhanoglu is another midfielder being looked at by the Bianconeri.

- Bayern Munich are considering moves for Liverpool pair Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz plus Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku as question marks hang over the futures of Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala, according to TEAMtalk. The Bavarians' long-running efforts to sign Ngumoha could be blocked as the Reds are close to finalising a new contract for the winger, their interest in Wirtz has never wavered and Doku's lack of Premier League starts could aid Bayern's chances. Olise is in the sights of Barcelona and Real Madrid while, according to Football Insider, Liverpool and Arsenal are long-term admirers of Musiala.

- AFC Bournemouth don't want to let Junior Kroupi leave in January and are demanding £100 million for the forward, according to talkSPORT. The 20-year-old is the subject of interest from Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, with the latter also looking at Manchester United's Marcus Rashford. Even so, the Cherries are determined to keep their France international until the summer at least, and Kroupi would favour a move to Paris Saint-Germain whenever he leaves the Vitality Stadium.

- The relationship between AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and Roc Nation chairman Jay-Z could help bring Real Madrid forward Endrick to San Siro, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports. Brazil international Endrick, who is represented by Roc Nation, has started just one match for Madrid so far this season as the 20-year-old is firmly behind Kylian Mbappé in the pecking order. The 20-year-old enjoyed a successful loan spell at Lyon in the second half of last season, a move which Milan -- owned by media and sports investor Cardinale -- could look to replicate this term.

Other
- AC Milan's search for somebody who can play left-back has seen them look at Manchester United's Noussair Mazraoui, Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, Frosinone's Gabriele Calvani and Bologna's Juan Miranda. (Calciomercato)

- Napoli are seriously considering Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee regardless of whether or not Lorenzo Lucca departs. (Sky Sports Italia)

- Juventus are looking at Atalanta's Gianluca Scamacca, Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth and Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta after Luciano Spalletti asked for a tall and physically imposing striker. (La Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Leeds United are in talks to extend Dominic Calvert-Lewin's contract amid interest from Manchester United. (Daily Mail)

- Brighton & Hove Albion are pushing to try to beat Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan to the signing of Atlético Mineiro centre-back Vitão. (TEAMtalk)

- Brighton, Bournemouth, Brentford, Nottingham Forest, Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Sunderland, Fulham and Everton are all looking at Cruzeiro centre-back Jonathan Jesus. (TEAMtalk)

- Roma are keen to sign Nottingham Forest winger Callum Hudson-Odoi on loan in January. (Football Insider)

- Newcastle United are tracking Ajax centre-back Dies Janse, who also has interest from three other Premier League clubs. (TEAMtalk)

- Atalanta sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli watched Eddy Kouadio during Monza's 3-0 win against Fiorentina. (Nicolo Schira)

- Bologna sporting director Marco Di Vaio was also at the match to watch Leonardo Colombo and Ebenezer Akinsanmiro. (Nicolo Schira)

Which two teams will face off inside Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis for the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup?

NBA Cup FAQ: Everything to know
What is the format?

NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season.

In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate.

The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition.

How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings?

Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out.

The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage.

The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule.

Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible.

Where are the semifinals and final being played?

In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.)

Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games?

Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest.

Which teams make up the groups?

To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. As a result, the following groups were drawn:

Toronto Raptors
Orlando Magic

Brooklyn Nets

East Group B

New York Knicks

Does one group stand out the most from the others?

East Group B is a monster.

All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James, when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis.

What do players get for winning?

In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association.

Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games?

There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team.

Will this have any impact on the playoffs?

Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted.

Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup?

The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled).

Previous NBA Cup champions

2025

New York Knicks defeat San Antonio Spurs, 124-113
Tournament MVP: Jalen Brunson, Knicks

2024

Milwaukee Bucks defeat Oklahoma City Thunder, 97-81
Tournament MVP: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bucks

2023

Los Angeles Lakers defeat Indiana Pacers, 123-109
Tournament MVP: LeBron James, Lakers

stories.headline: Cale Makar rejoining Avalanche lineup after 'fluke' injury
stories.summary: The Avalanche are getting one of their stars back as defenseman Cale Makar returns to the lineup after missing three games with a lower-body injury.
stories.body:
DENVER -- The Colorado Avalanche are getting one of their stars back as defenseman Cale Makar returns to the lineup Wednesday night after missing three games with a lower-body injury.

"Feel good," Makar reported after morning skate as the Avalanche prepared to play Dylan Larkin and the Montreal Canadiens. "Ready to go."

It's going to be a while longer before standout forward Nathan MacKinnon takes to the ice. His timeline for a return from a lower-body injury was recently extended to 12 weeks.

MacKinnon and Makar both left in the second period of the Avalanche's 4-3 overtime loss in Ottawa on Nov. 12.

MacKinnon went down to his knees holding his right hip after being pushed while trying to gain control of the puck. Makar left favoring his right leg and explained Wednesday that he was taking the puck up the ice when he tweaked something.

"Just one of those kind of fluke things," Makar said. "Got to let it calm down for a bit. Haven't had it for a while."

The two-time Norris Trophy winner as the NHL's top defenseman has five goals and 18 assists in 19 games this season. He is averaging more than 22 minutes on the ice and ready to take on that kind of workload.

"Anytime you come back from an injury, you've got to be ready to go," Makar said. "Regardless if I'm playing 30 [minutes], if I'm playing 15, whatever team needs me for, I'll be there for it."

Avalanche coach Jared Bednar echoed that, saying "He's cleared to play. He's going to play."

Because of a quirk in the schedule, the Avalanche haven't played since a 4-0 win over the Anaheim Ducks on Thursday. They were 2-1 with Makar out.

"A little bit weird," Makar said of the prolonged break. "To be out for two weeks-ish and really miss ... three games, I'll take it."

Makar is ready to help pitch in to make up for the absence of MacKinnon, who has 10 goals and 20 assists this season.

"Obviously to lose a big piece like Nate, it's tough," Makar said. "It's a hard role to fill. We're not looking to fill it, but everybody's obviously got to step up."

stories.headline: MLB sues players' union, asking court to declare lockout legal
stories.summary: Major League Baseball sued its players' association in federal court Wednesday, asking that the league's contemplated lockout next week be declared legal.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Major League Baseball sued its players' association in federal court Wednesday, asking that the league's contemplated lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt for the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case.

In a 38-page complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, MLB and the corporate entities owning its 30 teams sued the Major League Baseball Players Association and the eight players on the union's executive subcommittee, including record-setting pitcher Tarik Skubal.

"MLB brings this action to keep the dispute over the next collective bargaining agreement ('CBA') at the bargaining table, where federal law says it belongs," the lawsuit states. "MLB has a reasonable and imminent fear that the Union will attempt to use the threat of antitrust liability to derail the collective bargaining process altogether in favor of antitrust litigation."

Baseball's five-year labor contract expires at 11:59 p.m. on Tuesday, Dec. 1, and owners are expected to immediately impose a lockout, which would be the sport's 10th work stoppage since 1972. Owners have proposed a salary cap for the first time since 1994, when players fought off the proposal with a 7½-month strike that led to the first cancellation of the World Series in 90 years.

Owners asked for a declaratory judgment determining that a lockout doesn't violate antitrust laws and doesn't amount to an unreasonable restraint of trade. They asked for a ruling that the federal courts lack jurisdiction to enjoin a lockout and for an order that the players be defined as a legal class, which if granted could block individual lawsuits.

"The lawsuit filed today by MLB is completely frivolous," the union said in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing."

Among the lawyers representing MLB are former U.S. Solicitor General Paul D. Clement and Keker, Van Nest & Peters, which worked on behalf of the union in litigation against government seizure of drug tests.

stories.headline: Source: MLS owners agree new 16-team playoff format starting in 2027-28
stories.summary: MLS team owners have agreed on a new playoff format for the 2027-28 season featuring 16 teams, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
Major League Soccer's team owners have agreed on a new playoff format for the 2027-28 season, one that will feature 16 teams with two rounds of home-and-home series and single elimination thereafter, a source with knowledge of the league's plans confirmed to ESPN.

The format was approved by team owners at the MLS Board of Governors meeting in Miami on Nov. 12. Aggregate goals will be used to determine the winners in the first two rounds with extra time and penalties used to break ties, though that approach could change, the source said.

The new approach to the postseason will be implemented in conjunction with the league's shift to a summer-to-spring calendar that more closely aligns with leagues in Europe.

The calendar transition will feature what is being called a "sprint season" to take place in the first half of 2027. That competition will feature a 14-game regular season, with the top eight teams from each conference qualifying for the playoffs. Each playoff round in that competition will be single elimination, culminating in MLS Cup on Memorial Day weekend.

The Athletic was the first to report the new playoff format. An official announcement is expected on Dec. 3. The source added that the new format was discussed with broadcast partners and sponsors.

The agreed-upon format for the 2027-28 season reflects a more simplified approach than what was previously being considered.

That previous format would have featured 20 teams in a double elimination system inspired by Australian Rules Football. The number of qualifiers received pushback from fans and media, with the league ultimately agreeing to scale back the number of teams reaching the postseason.

MLS has frequently modified its playoff format over the course of its existence, oscillating between best-of-three and home-and-home series, as well as whether away goals counted as a tiebreaker.

Currently the league uses a system in which 18 teams reach the postseason. A preliminary wild card round involving four teams feeds into a 16-team setup featuring a best-of-three series in the conference quarterfinal round. The conference semifinal, conference final and MLS Cup final are all single elimination.

Part of what drove consideration for the Aussie Rules format was increasing the inventory of playoff games, which typically draw the best ratings. The new format will still contain a total of 27 playoff games. The current approach features between 25 and 33 games. Reducing the number of playoff teams from 18 to 16 will also place more emphasis on the regular season.

The source also confirmed that the 2027-28 regular season will feature a revised format. Teams will be split among five divisions, and will play each of their division rivals twice, and the remainder of the teams in the league once for a total of 34 games.

While the final details still need to be approved, the league is looking at playoff qualification being determined partly by how a team finishes in its division, as well as a league-wide table. Five of the games against division rivals will take place at the end of the season to add some drama to the fight for playoffs places.

stories.headline: Williams, Alpine fined £627k by FIA for breaching F1's cost cap
stories.summary: The FIA has announced that Williams overspent by £627,000 under F1's cost cap last year, while Williams and Alpine both committed "procedural" breaches.
stories.body:
The FIA has announced that Williams overspent by £627,000 ($821, 869) under Formula 1's cost cap last year, while Williams and Alpine both committed "procedural" breaches under the sport's financial regulations for 2025.

The two teams have accepted the findings of the FIA's Cost Cap Administration (CCA) and entered into accepted breach agreements (ABAs), by which each team acknowledges their overstep and agrees to a penalty.

Williams will face a financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in its wind tunnel and CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) time next year, while Alpine will only face a financial penalty.

Williams overspent by £627,000 last year, which equates to a 0.48% breach of the 2025 budget cap.

In a statement released by the FIA, the CCA recognised the following points.

"There is no accusation or evidence that WGPE [Williams Grand Prix Engineering] sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the Cost Cap Administration.

"The Financial Regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by WGPE in good faith; WGPE has accepted the FIA's interpretation and the resulting breaches.

"There is no evidence that WGPE gained or sought to gain any advantage (sporting or otherwise) from the identified breaches; and the Minor Overspend Breach amounts to £627k and therefore, with 0.48% over the 2025 Cost Cap, falls at the lower end of the

Williams also issued a statement acknowledging the breach.

"Atlassian Williams F1 Team has reached an Accepted Breach Agreement with the FIA in relation to our 2025 Cost Cap submission," the team statement said.

"The FIA has determined that the team committed a minor overspend breach and an accompanying procedural breach, unintentionally exceeding the cap by £627,000 - 0.48% over the 2025 Cost Cap. The agreed outcome is a financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months.

"The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

"The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

"Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future.

"We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the Cost Cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective."

Although Alpine did not overspend in 2025, its financial reporting included inaccuracies relating to marketing activities, non-F1 activities, HR activities, employee bonus costs, offsetting of costs and costs of inventories.

As with Williams, the FIA made clear that Alpine had not acted in a fraudulent manner nor sought to gain an advantage.

Alpine accepted the findings, and its financial penalty, in a statement of its own.

"BWT Alpine Formula One Team acknowledges and accepts the findings of the Cost Cap Administration (CCA) for the 2025 Reporting Period," the statement said. "The team accepts that it unknowingly committed a Procedural Breach, which is a result of inaccuracies in the Full Year Reporting Documentation for costs related to exclusions and adjustments.

"The errors and inaccuracies in the reporting were specifically related to non-sporting and operational costs which the CCA recognised didn't give the team any performance advantage, such as Marketing Activities, non-F1 Activities, HR Activities, Employee's Bonus Costs, Offsetting of Costs, and Costs of Inventories.

"The team would also like to express its thanks to both the CCA and FIA, for its diligence and understanding throughout the entire process. The Financial Regulations are still relatively new, constantly evolving and complex, with some exclusions and adjustments being open to each team's interpretation. The team acknowledges the collective efforts it needs to make across the business and recognises where improvements can be made in future."

The other nine F1 teams were found to be in compliance with the 2025 financial regulations.

F1 introduced its cost cap in 2021 to make the series more sustainable and provide a more level the playing field between the biggest teams and the sport's backmarkers.

Red Bull was found to be in breach of the very first cost cap after it emerged it had overspent by 1.6% in 2021, resulting in a $7 million fine for the team and a 10% reduction in its wind tunnel and CFD time.

stories.headline: Sparks forward Cameron Brink, Ben Felter wed at Stanford
stories.summary: The couple met in 2021 and was engaged in 2024 before marrying at their alma mater's Memorial Church.
stories.body:
Cameron Brink and Ben Felter have officially tied the knot after holding a ceremony on Nov. 14 at their alma mater Stanford's Memorial Church.

According to a report Tuesday from Vogue Magazine, which shared behind-the-scenes details and images, the Los Angeles Sparks forward had four bridal looks, including a custom dress from bridal designer Danielle Frankel for the ceremony, and another for the reception.

Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha, were among those in attendance. Curry and Brink are godsiblings as their fathers were teammates at Virginia Tech, and their mothers were roommates on campus.

The reception was at Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, while vows were exchanged at Memorial Church, one of the earliest interdenominational churches in the West. The waiting list to get married there can be up to four years, but alumni receive a shorter period, according to Vogue. The couple told the magazine that they always knew they wanted to wed there.

"Walking past the ornate mosaics on my way to class was always the best part of my day," Brink said.

Brink and Felter met at Stanford in the fall of 2020. The two began dating in March 2021 after Felter sent Brink an email in which he included his phone number. Felter, who rowed at Stanford, proposed to Brink in Paris in September 2024.

The No. 2 pick in the 2024 WNBA draft, Brink averaged a career-high 9.5 points plus five rebounds and 1.8 blocks for Los Angeles in the 2026 season.

stories.headline: Navajo Stirling belts another former champ, moves up in rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
If you've ever worn a UFC light heavyweight championship belt, watch out for Navajo Stirling.

His two most recent victories have come against former 205-pound champions, both knockouts. After a first-round finish of Jan Blachowicz in August, the New Zealander knocked out Jiří Procházka in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar.

As a result, Stirling leapfrogs Procházka in the ESPN divisional rankings, rising to No. 3 at light heavyweight. After his fourth straight knockout overall, Stirling (12-0) is right behind the division's champion, Carlos Ulberg, Stirling's training partner at City Kickboxing in Auckland. The No. 1 ranking belongs to former champion Magomed Ankalaev, who called out Stirling after Saturday's fight.

The weekend's UFC fights also led to changes in the featherweight and men's flyweight top 10s. Aljamain Sterling lost a 145-pound fight to Kevin Vallejos and drops four spots to No. 7, right below Vallejos. At 125 pounds, Kyoji Horiguchi moves up one position to No. 6 after beating Asu Almabayev, who remains 10th.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

stories.headline: Price tag for Tassie's new AFL stadium goes up, again
stories.summary: The estimated cost of a new 23,000-seat waterfront venue, set to eventually become the home of the Tasmania Devils, has risen again.
stories.body:
Tasmania's new AFL stadium has suffered another cost blowout, causing the premier to break a promise to cap the state's spend as critics fear the end price will be far higher.

The cost estimate for the 23,000-seat roofed venue at Macquarie Point in Hobart has increased from $1.13 billion to $1.23 billion.

On top of the figure is $132 million for broader precinct infrastructure, project delivery costs of $183 million and unspecified contingencies, taking the total to $1.54 billion.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff previously pledged to cap Tasmania's contribution to the build at $875 million as part of a deal to get the project through parliament.

But he conceded on Tuesday the state would have to cover the slated $100 million increase via extra borrowings.

"The previous cost estimate, which we announced ... some 14 months ago, there's been a lot of water under the bridge since that point," Mr Rockliff said.

The premier confirmed the project wouldn't head back to parliament for the approval of the necessary extra funding, despite previous assurances it would.

The latest estimate reflects increases in the cost of construction, sustained high oil and materials prices, higher labour costs and its complexity, the state government said.

The stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031 AFL season and was a condition of the Tasmania Devils being granted a licence to enter into the national competition in 2028.

It initially had a price tag of $715 million.

Mr Rockliff said the state had reached out to the federal government and AFL for extra money on top of their $240 million and $15 million contributions.

Anti-stadium group Our Place Hobart said the new cost estimate failed to take into account other factors, including the interest bill and the exact cost of contingencies.

Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff described the ongoing cost increases as a deep betrayal of Tasmanians.

"Who knows where the final price for the stadium will end up?" she said.

"What we do know is there's been now a fifth major cost blowout and there's not yet a contract price locked in for this massive project."

Federal independent MP Andrew Wilkie fears the stadium will end up costing $2 billion.

"Once you add the cost of the debt over a decade, the total cost to the Tasmanian taxpayer is closer to $3.5 billion," he said.

Devils chief executive Brendon Gale said the question of any additional funding from the AFL was a matter for the sport's governing body.

"The politicians can politic. We'll get on with building our club," he said.

"People have their views and are entitled to them. But based on my experience, people never look back. These types of projects transform cities and states."

The release of updated costs came ahead of schedule after the government bowed to political pressure to make the figures public before the end of the parliamentary year.

In mid-October, BESIX Watpac was announced as the preferred builder. A final contract is set to be signed by the end of 2026.

BESIX Watpac recently built a 30,000-seat roofed stadium in Christchurch in New Zealand which cost about $540 million.

Mr Rockliff said the final contract price for the Hobart stadium was unlikely to differ from the $1.23 billion estimate.

The stadium has been deeply divisive in Tasmania amid rising state debt, a stretched health system and other under-pressure services.

The AFL and federal government have been contacted for comment.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."

stories.headline: Best bets and top prop plays for Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills
stories.summary: Odds, analysis and picks to help you bet Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving.
stories.body:
Thanksgiving Day gives us a trifecta of NFL games. The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions get the day started in a game that has the highest total of Week 12.

Next up is a rematch between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys won the first matchup between NFC East rivals and are sizable favorites in the rematch.

The Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills close out the day in what is one of the best matchups of the season.

Let's get on to the analysis and best bets for the games. (You can find odds for every Week 12 game here.)

Jump to:

Bears-Lions | Eagles-Cowboys | Chiefs-Bills

Chicago and Detroit enter Thanksgiving with identical 8-2 records, and the winner will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North. The Bears have won five straight, while the Lions have won six consecutive games. Ben Johnson returns to Detroit, where former boss Dan Campbell has had plenty of success against Chicago.

The biggest challenge for the Bears will be containing Jahmyr Gibbs. He has rushed for 251 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games, and Chicago ranks 25th in yards per carry allowed. Jeffery Simmons has helped improve the Bears' defensive front, but slowing Gibbs will be critical.

Chicago has favorable matchups of its own. Detroit has struggled against quarterbacks and tight ends, which should benefit Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland. With Cole Kmet out for the season, Loveland remains a major part of the passing game, despite seeing only three targets against the Saints in Week 11.

Both offenses have the personnel to put up points, but Detroit's running game and Chicago's ability to contain explosive plays could determine the outcome. I'm leaning toward the Lions on the moneyline at home.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Jahmyr Gibbs rushing yards OVER 92.5 (-114)

Gibbs has rushed for 251 yards over his last two games, handling 45 carries during that stretch. He has surpassed 92.5 rushing yards in five of his last six games and faces a Bears defense ranked 25th in yards per carry allowed. Detroit should continue leaning on Gibbs, especially against Chicago's improved pass rush. Gibbs' recent workload gives him a good chance to clear this number.

Colston Loveland receiving yards OVER 53.5 (-112)

Loveland saw just three targets against New Orleans, but his playing time remained encouraging. He played 57 of Chicago's 61 offensive snaps and ran routes on 25 of 27 passing plays. He has averaged 7.4 targets over his last five games and should remain one of Williams' top receiving options. Detroit has allowed the third-most receiving yards per game to tight ends, giving Loveland a favorable matchup to bounce back.

Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns in last week's 51-30 win over the Titans, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 234 receiving yards and two scores. Philadelphia's secondary could have trouble containing both receivers, especially with Quinyon Mitchell dealing with a hamstring injury and Jonathan Jones (ankle) sidelined in practice.

The Eagles improved to 3-7 after beating the Steelers, but their passing game continues to struggle without Jalen Hurts. Joe Milton has averaged just 155 passing yards in two starts and has yet to throw a touchdown pass.

On the positive side, DeVonta Smith drew 12 targets against Pittsburgh in his return to the lineup and played 81% of the snaps. Saquon Barkley handled a season-high 17 carries and should have opportunities against a Dallas defense that has struggled against running backs.

I lean toward Dallas covering, but the spread gives me some hesitation. The Cowboys have struggled with consistency this season, and Philadelphia's defensive front has the ability to pressure Prescott and keep the game competitive.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

George Pickens receiving yards OVER 69.5 (-114)

Pickens had 18 receptions for 247 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games. The Eagles' injury situation gives him an opportunity to continue that production. Mitchell's availability for Philadelphia will be key, but Pickens' recent target volume and production put him in a good spot to clear this line.

DeVonta Smith receptions OVER 5.5 (-107)

Smith caught just five passes last week, but the target volume was encouraging. Dallas has struggled against wide receivers, and the Cowboys being favored by more than a touchdown could force Philadelphia to throw the football. Milton's accuracy remains the biggest concern with Smith's prop. With that said, the target volume makes it worth considering.

Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have developed one of the league's most entertaining quarterback rivalries, but Thursday's game could be decided by the running backs.

Buffalo ranks second in rushing yards per game, with James Cook III and Allen both capable of making plays on the ground. Cook has 10 rushing touchdowns this season for the Bills, who lead the league in rushing scores.

Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (groin) will miss his third straight game, but Emmett Johnson has been productive in his absence, recording consecutive 100-yard rushing performances.

Weather could also impact Thursday night's game. Rain and gusty winds are forecast for Orchard Park, potentially making it difficult to throw downfield.

I lean under 46.5, but I wouldn't chase the number much lower. Mahomes and Allen are capable of creating explosive plays, even in difficult conditions, and turnovers could give either team short fields.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

James Cook III anytime touchdown (-105)

Cook has scored 10 rushing touchdowns in 10 games, and Buffalo leads the league with 21 rushing scores. Rain and windy conditions could lead to additional rushing attempts against Kansas City, although the Chiefs have been difficult to run against. Allen also remains a threat near the goal line, but Cook's workload -- he averaged 105.6 rushing yards over his last five games -- and touchdown production make him a reasonable option at these odds.

Josh Allen rushing yards OVER 36.5 (-111)

Allen has rushed for 506 yards in 10 career games against the Chiefs, including the playoffs, averaging 50.6 yards per game. And he has cleared this line in seven of those matchups. With the forecast, Allen could see more designed runs and scrambles. He has surpassed this number just twice in 10 games this season, but he has consistently been more aggressive as a runner against Kansas City. I'm betting that continues on Thanksgiving.

stories.headline: Champions League recap: Another night of mayhem for Pochettino's Man United
stories.summary: Manchester United's winless run continued as another day of UEFA Champions League action unfolded across Europe.
stories.body:
The Champions!

Matchday 5 of the UEFA Champions League continued Wednesday, with nine more matches across the continent as the race for a place in the knockout rounds continues to heat up!

In our two early matches, Barcelona traveled to Azerbaijan and cruised to a 4-1 win over Sabah while Villarreal secured a 1-0 victory away at Slavia Prague.

Later in the standout matches, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain faced off against AS Roma as the match ended in a 2-2 draw, while Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United continued winless as they went to Portugal to take on Sporting CP in the Argentine's first Champions League match in charge of the club, only for that match to also end in a 2-2 draw.

Elsewhere, Liverpool visited Club Brugge and got all three points in a 3-0 win while Bayern Munich took on Lille in France, with the Ligue 1 side securing its first victory of the Champions League campaign in stunning fashion with a 2-1 win.

Other results had Atlético Madrid defeating Viking 2-0, Internazionale defeating Stuttgart 2-0 and Fenerbahçe defeating Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0.

Enjoy all that happened from Wednesday's matches across Europe!

stories.headline: Nottingham Forest boss Glasner hits out at players who don't learn English
stories.summary: Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said standards at the club were not good enough when he took charge.
stories.body:
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said standards at the club were not good enough when he took charge, reserving specific criticism for players he said have failed to learn English despite being at the Premier League club for several years.

Forest have won just two of their 11 Premier League games since Glasner took charge this summer, becoming the club's fifth head coach in less than a year.

"Stability in a company is having standards," Glasner told a news conference on Wednesday. "Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

"We have players who are here for four years, [who] can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

"For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English. If I want to manage in Italy, I have to speak Italian."

Forest are out of the Premier League's bottom three but only on goal difference as they welcome Chelsea to the City Ground on Friday night.

They have played well in patches, beating Manchester City and Aston Villa, while also drawing at Liverpool, but their campaign has been littered with errors.

Glasner said he expected a better start, but knows it will take hard work.

"We have just two wins after 11 games. We wanted and expected more from us, to be honest, but that's the reality," Glasner told a news conference ahead of the game.

"For me, it's always accepting the reality and now having a look at what we need to improve and work on. That's the only way.

"I'm no magician. I have no magician dust I can spread somewhere at the training ground. My experience is it takes hard work, especially in the Premier League.

"We need to improve our individual mistakes -- we make too many in defence and then you get punished in the Premier League.

"We need to improve our efficiency in attack and we definitely need to improve our set-pieces, because it's still no goal from a set-piece."

Winger Callum Hudson-Odoi is fit to face his former club.

- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving

- Transfer rumors, news: Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes eyed by Juventus

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Newcastle eye Inter's Pio Esposito

Hudson-Odoi missed Saturday's 2-0 defeat at AFC Bournemouth with an injury picked up during the international break, but he is back involved for the visit of Xabi Alonso's side.

He remains unlikely to start, though, having played just 76 minutes in all competitions this season as he has found trying to fit into Glasner's system tough.

Forest are without Nicolás Domínguez and Nicolò Savona.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand returning from injuries against Senators
stories.summary: Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are about to be in the Panthers' lineup together for the first time since the title-clinching game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final.
stories.body:
Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are about to be in the Florida Panthers' lineup together for the first time since the title-clinching game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final, which was more than 17 months ago.

The Panthers made the announcement Wednesday morning that both are returning from knee injuries and expected to play against the Ottawa Senators.

"They're back," the team said in a social media post.

The returns were not unexpected, though Marchand's might have come a few days before the Panthers initially anticipated. Florida made some roster adjustments this week to free up cap space needed to get both into the lineup, the clearest sign that the returns were close.

"It's just the excitement of the unknown. We have no idea what we look like with both these guys in our lineup," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. "The core guys haven't played together since June of '25. So there is that excitement. In some ways feels like the season starts today."

Both Barkov and Marchand had appeared in only two of Florida's first 24 games this season. Barkov played the first two, Marchand played the next two, and both got hurt during their second contests of the campaign. Late November was always the target for both, and they evidently hit the rehab finish line together.

Barkov missed all of last season because of ligament tears in his right knee. He played in Florida's first two games this season, both on the road, before hurting his left knee Oct. 1. Marchand made his season debut Oct. 4 then hurt his knee in a game two days later.

Both have been practicing for much of November.

"You can survive short-term injuries and you can keep your culture, you can keep your identity," Maurice said. "You cannot take your best player out for 100 games and keep a lot of that. So we have to rebuild our identity now."

Marchand, 38, is in his third season with the Panthers after playing his first 16 seasons with the rival Boston Bruins. He was traded to Florida in March 2025 and helped the Panthers win their second straight Stanley Cup that season.

"Brad's been in and out of the lineup, and he's just been so good for us when he's in," Maurice said. "Even last year, fairly close to a point a game and he was hurt most of that time. He's prolific."

Barkov, 31, is Florida's all-time leader in goals, assists and points. He was the team's leader in games played as well, but since getting hurt he has ceded that spot to Panthers defenseman Aaron Ekblad.

"It's huge," Panthers defenseman Niko Mikkola said of Barkov. "He's the face of the team, the leader and probably our most important player."

stories.headline: Paul Goldschmidt says time with Yankees prepared him for expectations Mets face
stories.summary: Paul Goldschmidt knew Mets manager Andy Green from their time together with Arizona in 2015 and was eager make the move across town from the Yankees to reunite.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Paul Goldschmidt knew New York Mets manager Andy Green from their time together with Arizona in 2015 and was eager make the move across town from the Yankees to reunite.

"It's an exciting team, a very talented team. I think there's really high expectations for this team," the first baseman said Wednesday after finalizing an $8 million, one-year contract with the Mets. "The expectations of this organization are to win the World Series from the outside looking in and I have no doubt that the players and coaches, front office, ownership feel that same way."

Green was Goldschmidt's third-base coach with the Diamondbacks in 2015, then left to become San Diego's manager. Green replaced Carlos Mendoza as Mets manager in June and was given a three-year contract in September.

"We always stayed in touch. I think he's really smart and he really has a game plan of how he wants to attack things," Goldschmidt said. "I remember him just being very open to continuing to learn. He didn't think he had all the answers and so, that's always very encouraging."

A seven-time All-Star who spent the past two seasons across town with the Yankees, the 39-year-old hit .252 with 18 homers, 52 RBI and a .765 OPS in 380 plate appearances over 105 games this year, then became a free agent.

As part of his Mets deal, Goldschmidt can earn an additional $2 million in performance bonuses for plate appearances: $500,000 each for 450 and 475, and $1 million for 500.

"Being with the other team in New York the last couple years, you know the expectations of this city," Goldschmidt said. "There was nothing that anyone really needed to sell me on. I knew that going in and so when they called it was exciting."

He's eager to team with Tarik Skubal, who has a pending $450 million, nine-year agreement with the Mets, a record for a pitcher.

"I got a chance to play with him on Team USA," Goldschmidt said, referring to this year's World Baseball Classic. "He was a great guy, a great leader and a competitor, and obviously an amazing pitcher."

Goldschmidt, the 2022 NL MVP with St. Louis, will likely platoon with left-handed-hitting first baseman Jared Young.

"My top concern was not: Hey, how do I go to someplace where I get the most playing time?" he said. "My concern was going to a team where it felt right."

A right-handed hitter, Goldschmidt batted .299 with 11 homers and a .967 OPS in 183 plate appearances against left-handed pitchers this year. He is a .322 career hitter versus lefties, with a 1.004 OPS.

"It's been fun to have a different perspective. It's kind of like a relief pitcher. You think you're going to come into the game in the fifth and you don't come into until the seventh," he said. "So it's like trying to find that balance of being ready so that the game doesn't sneak up."

Goldschmidt is a four-time Gold Glove winner with a .286 average, 390 home runs, 1,284 RBIs and an .877 OPS in 16 major league seasons with the Diamondbacks, Cardinals and Yankees.

"I enjoyed playing in New York. When I was a visiting player, you enjoy the adrenaline that comes with these games, with the energy that you can feel in the stadium," he said. "The No. 1 thing I would just say about this city is the high expectations of both these teams and really all the sports teams and really anything that goes on in New York."

stories.headline: Luis Suárez says 'no excuses left' as Miami looks to avoid early playoff exit
stories.summary: Luis Suárez said there are "no excuses left" for Inter Miami as the defending MLS Cup champion stares at a possible first-round playoff exit.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- Luis Suárez said there are "no excuses left" for Inter Miami as the defending MLS Cup champion stares at a possible first-round elimination from this year's MLS playoffs.

Miami lost 3-0 to the Columbus Crew in the first game of the round one best-of-three series at home on Saturday. Suárez and Co. must now win Game 2 on Friday to ensure a decisive third game back in Miami and avoid immediate elimination.

"It's clear that at a club like this, we have an obligation to win, getting eliminated on Friday would be a disappointment, and that's how we should see it," Suárez said on Wednesday.

"There are no excuses left, not the pitch, not fatigue, nothing. It's time to face reality. If we do get knocked out, we'll be the first to be self-critical. But let's hope that doesn't happen, because we are the ones primarily responsible, we're the ones out there on the pitch.

"The coach can provide the tools, but the decisions and the actions on the field are entirely up to us. Every single player needs to take that responsibility. Everyone knows what they can contribute this Friday; we need 150%, even 200%, from every one of us to bring this series back home."

Seeded second in the Eastern Conference after a rollercoaster season, Miami was dominated by seventh-seeded Columbus in Game 1 at Nu Stadium. But coach Cristian "Kily" González insisted that an immediate exit would not be a failure.

"It would be a disappointment, but not a failure, this is football, after all," González, who took charge of Miami in September, told a news conference on Wednesday. "A true failure would be not trying at all. We are trying, sometimes well, sometimes not so well.

"That's just life: sometimes things go well, sometimes they don't."

Miami entered the playoffs as reigning MLS champion after defeating the Vancouver Whitecaps in last year's final. But the team is no stranger to first-round elimination, having fallen to Atlanta United in three games in 2024 despite setting a then-points record during the regular season.

"I know that, as a team, and as the reigning champions, it is our responsibility and our obligation to advance," González added. "It's not about feeling pressured. It's about recognizing where we stand and knowing we are prepared to go all the way.

"I don't look at it in terms of failure; I always envision us moving forward. I said as much after our last match, and I remain convinced that's how it will play out. We've prepared as best we could, even with the rain preventing us from training on the pitch, we've already put in the necessary work."

While a star-studded lineup led by back-to-back MLS Golden Boot winner Lionel Messi increases expectations in Miami, González said it also adds to the motivation for its rivals.

"Everyone wants to beat us," he said. "Every team plays differently against us; why? Because you have the world's number one, and because you know the repercussions that brings, so we have to come to terms with that."

"You have to accept that every team will try to beat you by any means necessary, no matter what. If you look at matches against other opponents, the game is played differently; against us, it's a whole other story, and you have to grasp that.

"So you have to be prepared, knowing that we're facing a final, our last chance, we're well aware of that."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen admits to 40-hour GTA VI spree as he won Las Vegas GP
stories.summary: Max Verstappen claims he had already clocked 40 hours of Grand Theft Auto VI before his brilliant Las Vegas Grand Prix win at the weekend.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen claims he had already clocked 40 hours of Grand Theft Auto VI before his brilliant Las Vegas Grand Prix win at the weekend.

Verstappen delivered a masterclass of how to race with F1's new engines to win in Sin City, a race which saw an incredible 35 lead changes, but has since revealed that much of his downtime was spent binging through Rockstar's highly-anticipated new game, which came out on Nov. 19.

Revealing the total gameplay time to teammates on the Twitch channel of his esports team, Verstappen Sim Racing, formerly known as Team Redline, he was then asked if his flight home felt like the quickest ever because of the game.

"No, I was sleeping on the plane," he replied. "I played a lot in the evening and the morning in Vegas."

The release of the game coincided with the start of the on-track schedule in Vegas.

Verstappen was one of the drivers who admitted during media day on Wednesday that he had already pre-downloaded the game ready to play, which came out at midnight leading into Thursday.

The schedule followed with two practice sessions on Nov. 19, then qualifying and the race at 8 p.m. local time on Nov. 20 and 21 respectively.

When one of his fellow Twitch streamers quipped it was time well spent, he added: "Yeah! It's not like I can go out anyway."

Verstappen later revealed he does not watch any of the cut scenes around the game's story.

"I'm over 80% of the missions," he added.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1

- Haas confirm Rafa Camara will finish 2026 season with the team

The admission will add another layer to what will likely go down as one of the best and most memorable grand prix performances of his storied career, which also included a brutal putdown of Mercedes rival George Russell, who he claimed is "so far below my level" that he was unfazed by criticism the British driver had made earlier in the week.

Verstappen is known for gaming at all hours during F1 weekends.

In 2024, Red Bull's then-racing advisor Helmut Marko had to ask the Dutchman to stop streaming himself playing late-night sim racing sessions with Team Redline in the middle of the night and early hours of the morning during F1 weekends.

Verstappen later said the yo-yo Vegas race was something he had only ever experienced playing Mario Kart before.

stories.headline: WNBA players elect Elizabeth Williams as union president
stories.summary: Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who had been in the role since 2016.
stories.body:
Chicago Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who retired after being in the role since 2016.

Williams, who will serve out the final two years of Ogwumike's term that began earlier this year, was picked by players on Tuesday over Breanna Stewart of the New York Liberty and Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, a source with knowledge of the ballot told ESPN.

A 12-year veteran, Williams joined the WNBPA executive committee in 2018 and served four two-year terms. She has been at the bargaining table for two CBAs, including the most recent agreement that raised maximum player salaries to over $1 million.

"One of my main goals as president is to increase the engagement of the younger members of this union," Williams said in a statement to WNBPA player representatives. "I know the value of diverse voices in these conversations. We may not always agree, but I want to make sure every player knows that her voice is being heard.

"This is the strength of our union. I am grateful for what we have accomplished over these last few years, and I'm excited about the potential for a new opportunity to serve."

The WNBA will also have a new face leading the league office as commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the year. A search for her replacement is ongoing.

Williams will lead the executive committee comprised of Napheesa Collier (1st vice president), Veronica Burton (secretary), Chelsea Gray (treasurer), and three additional vice presidents: Alysha Clark, Ezi Magbegor, and Maya Caldwell.

Burton, Gray, Magbegor and Caldwell join the executive committee for the first time.

"These election results reflect the strength of our union and the power of player leadership," WNBPA executive director Terri Carmichael Jackson said in a statement. "Congratulations to Elizabeth and each of our newly elected and returning Executive Committee members, whose collective experience, diverse perspectives, and commitment will help guide the WNBPA into its next chapter.

"As we turn our focus to implementing our transformational CBA and building on the progress our members have fought so hard to achieve, our greatest strength remains our unity, our democratic process, and our unwavering commitment to one another."

Williams, who was selected fourth overall in the 2015 WNBA draft out of Duke and was the 2016 Most Improved Player, becomes president after a lengthy period of stability in union leadership.

Ogwumike, the outgoing WNBPA president, announced her WNBA retirement during the 2026 season. An 11-time All-Star and the 2016 MVP, Ogwumike has served as WNBPA president since 2016, presiding over two collective bargaining agreement negotiations and shaping the social justice activism that defined the player body during her tenure.

stories.headline: Heeney headlines returning Swans at pre-season training
stories.summary: After months of off-field turmoil in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal, the Sydney Swans have welcomed back four AFL players for pre-season training.
stories.body:
The Sydney Swans have welcomed back their embattled AFL quartet to training after months of off-field turmoil following the Pullman Hotel scandal.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice signalled their intent to resurrect their playing careers by taking part in the club's first-to-fourth-year pre-season training on Monday.

High-profile forward Tom Papley was also in attendance at Sydney's Bat and Ball Oval after being slapped with a three-game ban by the AFL for a positive roadside drug test.

Monday's session marked the first time Heeney, Warner, Bice and Jordon have officially trained with the Swans since serving a season-ending suspension for what the club termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

That AFL-endorsed suspension was also served by now-North Melbourne player Nick Blakey.

Separate from the bans, Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey were under investigation after three women made reports of sexual assault to Victoria Police.

Police have since confirmed the players would not be charged due to insufficient evidence.

Civil claims are still being prepared against relevant parties.

Monday's session was a relaxed affair, with the club also welcoming draftees Caylen Murray, Mason McGroder, Mitchell Knevitt and Brady Wright.

Players undertook the usual pre-season conditioning programs, doing running drills before moving on to contest work and a short match simulation.

It wasn't the first time Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Rice had trained with teammates, having done informal sessions at Centennial Park.

Papley, one of the team's most experienced players, returned to training as he prepares to face Waverley Local Court for driving with a suspended licence on November 26.

The 30-year-old was pulled over by NSW Police for a random roadside drug test on November 2, with checks revealing his licence was suspended due to non-payment of a parking fine.

The initial roadside test returned a positive reading, and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken.

That secondary sample returned a positive roadside test for the presence of cocaine and MDMA.

On top of his AFL ban for conduct unbecoming, Papley was fined $722 by police and his licence will be suspended for three months.

Papley spent most of Monday's training session with the rehabilitation group alongside fellow forwards Logan McDonald and Hayden McLean after undergoing surgery on both knees.

He suffered a grade-two medial collateral ligament strain in his right knee in the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, before undergoing an arthroscopy on his left knee to address a historic issue.

Papley will miss all pre-season matches and the club's opening rounds against Geelong, Essendon and GWS.

stories.headline: 'Little disappointing': Munster makes call on Storm offer
stories.summary: Melbourne's fight to keep Cameron Munster and Harry Grant has been made harder after the former rejected the club's latest offer.
stories.body:
Cameron Munster has declared all options are on the table after officially rejecting a deal to stay in Melbourne and labelling the Storm's latest offer as "disappointing".

With Melbourne already facing a battle to retain Harry Grant, the Storm are now officially fighting a retention war on two fronts after Munster's call.

The Melbourne superstar admitted on Tuesday that Grant's future could play a role in his own call, as well as Craig Bellamy's impending retirement at the end of 2027.

As it stands Munster will not take up an offer from the Storm that is understood to have been for one year with an option for a second.

"I have declined it," the Queensland State of Origin captain said at a Maroons sponsor announcement with Westpac.

"I am not saying I am going to leave Melbourne. Just with the terms and conditions that they put out to me, it is probably something that is a little disappointing.

"But it's a business, I am not stupid."

Munster admitted his own form had not been good enough for the Storm last season as they missed the finals for the first time in his career.

And in turn, the 32-year-old conceded the offer may have been as a result of that.

"That (offer) just makes my job a little bit harder. But it's also a bit of a challenge saying I am not where I need to be," he said.

"Maybe I need to be a little bit better to earn that contract that we're looking from.

"And maybe it is a little bit of a kick up the bum from them. I am not too sure where we'll go from here but all options are open at the moment."

Munster's rejection comes after Grant met with Gold Coast officials last Friday and officially received an offer to join the Titans.

It is understood Melbourne's offer for the Queensland dummy-half will either be worth similar or more than the Titans.

But Gold Coast are hopeful of luring the hooker north, given his relationship with ex-Maroons assistant coach Josh Hannay and prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui.

The Titans officially released AJ Brimson to the PNG Chiefs on Tuesday on a three-year deal, with the money from the centre used to help pursue Grant.

NSW prop Stefano Utoikamanu is also off contract at Melbourne at the end of next year and has also been linked to the Sydney Roosters.

At the same time Bellamy's retirement at the end of next season is proving a challenge for the Storm, given he is like a father figure to Munster.

"When you look at someone like Craig as a coach, he is a great coach and I have so much respect and have admired him for such a long time," Munster said.

"It's going to be different at the club. I'm not too sure where the club wants to go with all that stuff.

"I don't know who they are going to get and I'm sure it will be a daunting job coming after him."

Munster also confirmed he will likely follow the Cameron Smith route and give away representative football at some point to focus on club duties.

"It definitely has (crossed my mind)," Munster said.

"The hard thing for me is giving up the captaincy.

"Once I start declining (I will look at it) and I thought I was declining. But after my last few games for the World Cup I am pretty confident I can get back to that."
